data.title: JANEL CORP 2026: Revenue $67.51M, EPS $1.63— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
JANEL CORP reported results for the 2026 quarter with revenue of $67.51M and diluted EPS of $1.63, compared with $49.15M and $0.67 in the prior-year quarter, driven by strength in Logistics and recent acquisitions.

Financial Highlights

Revenue¹$67.51M$49.15M37.4%

Business Highlights

  • Revenue growth was driven by Logistics, which benefited from higher freight rates, improved net revenue per shipment and a favorable service mix that boosted margins.
  • Acquisition-led expansion contributed materially: Interlog and other deals grew Logistics scale, while majority stakes and asset purchases (including Biosensis, Rubicon and the BioPorto asset and a royalty) expanded Life Sciences and Manufacturing capabilities.
  • Logistics delivered strong organic gross profit growth and operating leverage; Life Sciences experienced timing-related order effects and inventory impacts from acquisitions.
  • Product and portfolio moves included adding antibody product lines, new royalties and integration of Rubicon to broaden Manufacturing distribution.

data.title: Immix Biopharma, Inc. Q2 2026: Net loss $(11.56)M, EPS $(0.18) — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Immix Biopharma, Inc. reported a larger consolidated net loss for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, with net income of $(11.56)M and diluted EPS of $(0.18); the company remains clinical-stage with no product revenue for the period.

Financial Highlights

  • Net income: $(11.56)M for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, versus $(6.62)M in the year-ago quarter.
  • Diluted EPS: $(0.18) for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, versus $(0.22) in the year-ago quarter.
  • Revenue: No product sales; company is clinical-stage and reports no revenue for the quarter.

Business Highlights

  • Clinical progress: Enrollment complete in NEXICART-2 (45 patients); Phase 1b/2 data show high complete response rates (95% of evaluable patients) and rapid responses.
  • Regulatory designations: NXC-201 received FDA Breakthrough Therapy, RMAT and orphan drug designations in the U.S. and EU, supporting an expedited development path.
  • R&D activity: Increased clinical R&D spending and higher CRO/site costs to support expanded trial operations and planned Phase 3 efforts.
  • Funding: Multiple equity offerings and CIRM grant reimbursements (~$8M) have funded trial progression and extended cash runway.
  • Safety profile: Favorable tolerability observed with no neurotoxicity and predominantly low-grade cytokine release syndrome, supporting broader development plans.

Original SEC Filing: Immix Biopharma, Inc. [ IMMX ] - 10-Q - Aug. 07, 2026

data.title: GYRE THERAPEUTICS, INC. Q2 2026: Revenue $29.11M, EPS $(0.12) — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
GYRE THERAPEUTICS, INC. reported second-quarter 2026 results with revenue of $29.11M, a slight decline from $29.73M a year earlier, and a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $(11.66)M, or $(0.12) diluted EPS, versus a net loss of $(2.04)M, or $(0.03) diluted EPS, in the year-ago quarter.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: $29.105M for Q2 2026, down from $29.734M in the year-ago quarter (−2.1% YoY).
  • Net income: Net loss attributable to common stockholders of $(11.663)M for Q2 2026, vs. net loss $(2.044)M in the year-ago quarter.
  • Diluted EPS: $(0.12) diluted EPS for Q2 2026, vs. $(0.03) diluted EPS in the year-ago quarter.

Business Highlights

  • Revenue & channel shift: Total revenue modestly declined year over year as higher ETUARY sales were largely offset by lower Contiva/Etorel revenue following China's centralized procurement.
  • Brand momentum: ETUARY and the newly commercialized Etorel strengthened their market positions in the PRC; ETUARY showed volume-driven growth in Q2 2026.
  • M&A and leadership: In May 2026 the company completed an all-stock acquisition of Cullgen (approximately $300M), adding roughly 740 employees and appointing Cullgen executives to CEO, CSO and CFO roles.
  • Pipeline progress: F351 met its Phase 3 primary endpoint for CHB liver fibrosis and the NDA was accepted by the NMPA in May 2026; multiple Cullgen degrader programs are advancing to or through Phase 1.
  • Operational spend & integration: R&D and transaction-related costs rose materially in H1 2026 to support F351 development and Cullgen integration, which weighed on operating results for the period.

Original SEC Filing: GYRE THERAPEUTICS, INC. [ GYRE ] - 10-Q - Aug. 07, 2026

data.title: Eightco Holdings Inc. 2Q 2026: Revenue $2.07M, Net income $17.7M — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Eightco Holdings Inc. reported results for the second quarter of 2026, with revenue of $2.07M and net income of $17.7M; revenue declined sharply year-over-year while reported net income benefited from a large fair-value gain on digital assets.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: $2.07M for 2Q 2026, down from $7.58M in the year-ago quarter ( (72.7% )YoY).
  • Net income: $17.70M for 2Q 2026, versus a net loss of $(1.17)M in the year-ago quarter (improvement driven by a $29.3M fair-value gain on digital assets).

Business Highlights

  • Revenue Trend: Forever 8 revenue fell 45–73% year-over-year, reflecting a sharp drop in orders from the company's largest customer.
  • Channel Shift: The company is transitioning away from an online retail/liquidation model toward inventory financing and strategic holdings.
  • Digital Asset Strategy: Management adopted a Digital Asset Treasury and deployed substantial proceeds into WLD/ETH holdings and other digital assets, which introduced material earnings volatility but provide liquidity options.
  • Customer Concentration Risk: Forever 8 remains highly concentrated, with approximately 99% of revenue from one customer, creating operational uncertainty.
  • Strategic Investments: Proceeds from an ATM offering were deployed into digital assets and private tech investments (including OpenAI and Beast Industries) to support the company's longer-term strategic shift.

Original SEC Filing: Eightco Holdings Inc. [ ORBS ] - 10-Q - Aug. 07, 2026

data.title: COLLECTIVE ACQUISITION CORP. Q2 2026: Net income $360K, EPS $0.02— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
COLLECTIVE ACQUISITION CORP. reported a Q2 2026 net income of $360K and diluted EPS of $0.02, down from $761K and $0.05, respectively, in the year-ago quarter as interest income from the Trust Account offset higher general and administrative expenses.

Financial Highlights

  • Net income was $360K for Q2 2026, down from $761K in Q2 2025.
  • Diluted earnings per share was $0.02 for Q2 2026, compared with $0.05 in Q2 2025.
  • Company attributed positive net results primarily to interest income from the Trust Account; higher G&A in Q2 2026 increased expenses versus the year-ago quarter.

Business Highlights

  • Blank-check SPAC focused on pursuing an initial Business Combination; no operating revenues are expected until a deal closes.
  • Activities during the quarter centered on target identification, due diligence, IPO preparation and organizational matters, funded by trust interest and sponsor loans.
  • Shareholders approved a one-year extension to complete a Business Combination to August 8, 2027.
  • Management transition: the CFO resigned and a new CFO was appointed effective July 17, 2026 to support the combination process.
  • Noted that new 2024 SEC SPAC rules may lengthen deal timelines and increase disclosure and compliance requirements for completing a Business Combination.

Original SEC Filing: COLLECTIVE ACQUISITION CORP. [ CCAQ ] - 10-Q - Aug. 07, 2026

data.title: Actinium Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Q2 2026: Revenue $35M, EPS $0.89— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Actinium Pharmaceuticals, Inc. reported second-quarter 2026 results with revenue of $35M and net income of $27.901M, driven primarily by recognition of a previously deferred $35M upfront license payment; diluted EPS was $0.89 for the quarter versus a loss of $(0.22) a year earlier.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $35.0M for Q2 2026, compared with $0 in Q2 2025; change driven by recognition of previously deferred $35M upfront license payment.
  • Net income was $27.901M for Q2 2026, compared with a net loss of $(6.878)M in Q2 2025; YoY change $34.779M.
  • Diluted EPS was $0.89 for Q2 2026, compared with $(0.22) for Q2 2025; YoY change $1.11.

Business Highlights

  • Revenue recognition: The company recognized a $35M previously deferred upfront license payment in June 2026, which drove quarter and year-to-date profitability.
  • R&D pipeline momentum: Advancing ATNM-400, Actimab-A and Iomab programs with multiple preclinical and clinical readouts planned in late 2026–2027.
  • Manufacturing scale-up: Completing a cGMP Ac-225 radiopharmaceutical facility and proprietary cyclotron Ac-225 production technology; facility expected to be operational in 2H 2026.
  • Clinical progress & partnerships: Ongoing Phase 1–3 trials (Iomab-B, Iomab-ACT, Actimab-A); NCI CRADA supports Actimab-A trials and cost-effective development.
  • Operational efficiency: Lower headcount reduced R&D and G&A costs; supply chain and distribution network expanded to about 50 cancer centers.

data.title: AVALON HOLDINGS CORP Q2 2026: Revenue $20.9M, EPS $0.23— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
AVALON HOLDINGS CORP reported second-quarter 2026 results with revenue of $20.9M, up from $20.3M a year earlier, and net income attributable to common shareholders of $0.88M, versus $0.27M in Q2 2025. Diluted earnings per share rose to $0.23 from $0.07 in the prior-year quarter.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: $20.9M for Q2 2026, compared with $20.3M in Q2 2025; YoY change 3.3%.
  • Net income: $0.88M attributable to common shareholders for Q2 2026, versus $0.27M in Q2 2025.
  • Diluted EPS: $0.23 for Q2 2026, compared with $0.07 in Q2 2025.

Business Highlights

  • Revenue growth was driven by waste services and stronger hospitality demand; year-to-date net operating revenues rose to $38.6M from $36.3M.
  • Waste management saw growth from increased continuous and event work; the captive landfill business remained stable while saltwater well operations remain suspended due to regulatory/legal matters.
  • Hospitality benefited from renovations at the Grand Resort, higher room rates and occupancy, which boosted hotel and food & beverage sales and supported membership and on-site spending.
  • Capital projects continue, including resort remodels, Squaw Creek pool expansion and clubhouse roof work, funded in phases from project fund cash.
  • Company operations face typical seasonality and risks from labor availability/costs and commodity volatility, along with ongoing regulatory and legal considerations related to saltwater well activities.

Original SEC Filing: AVALON HOLDINGS CORP [ AWX ] - 10-Q - Aug. 07, 2026

data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Toronto, Ontario – TheNewswire – August 7, 2026 - Ventripoint Diagnostics Ltd. ("Ventripoint" or the "Company") (TSXV:VPT; OTC:VPTDF) announces that it incorrectly granted 7,246,250 stock options of the Company to various officers, employees and consultants of the Company during the period of February 27, 2025 to May 27, 2026 as the Company did not obtain the necessary annual shareholder approval for the Company’s stock option plan. The Company had previously cancelled 250,000 option grants which will not be re-granted and effective June 30, 2026 has cancelled 4,301,250 option grants (the “Cancelled Options”), which included 1,000,000 options granted to an officer of the company. The Company has re-granted 3,151,250 of the cancelled options including 1,000,000 to an officer of the company and granted 3,241,500 annual incentive option grants to directors, officers, employees and consultants of the Company, which included 1,500,000 to officers and directors, at the current market price on July 8, 2026 under the stock option plan, which was approved at the Company’s recent shareholder meeting on May 27, 2026.  A total of 6,392,750 were granted at an exercise price of $0.095 for terms of 2 to 10 years and vesting immediately to over 3 years.  The company has 13.7 million options issued at a volume-weighted average exercise price of $0.16. and 5.0 million options available for future grants.

    The Company also announces that the grant and exercise of an aggregate of 2,695,000 stock options to various employees and consultants of the Company will be treated as a non-brokered private placement at prices ranging from $0.10 to $0.12, with an effective closing date of July 29, 2026, subject to TSXV acceptance.

    Out of 2,000,000 options granted on June 2, 2025, 1,190,000 options were exercised at a price of $0.10 and will be included in the private placement.

    Out of 1,370,000 options granted on June 12, 2025, 900,000 options were exercised at a price of $0.11 and will be included in the private placement.

    Out of 2,585,000 options granted on October 14, 2025, 380,000 options were exercised at a price of $0.11 and will be included in the private placement.

    Out of 291,250 options granted on December 30, 2025, 225,000 options were exercised at a price of $0.12 and will be included in the private placement.
